summary: Michael Kowalewski is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge from 1969 to 1972 and at SOAS University of London from 1987 to 1990.

Michael L. Walter (1947–2020) worked in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Larry William Moses and held positions at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 1982 and 2020) and the Lumbini International Research Institute (attested 2000).

Michael Lessman researches religious studies and Indology. He studied at Georgetown University, the Catholic University of America, the University of Munich, and Yale University, where he became a doctoral candidate in 2019.

Michael M. Ames (1933–2006) specialized in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of British Columbia and Harvard University under Cora Du Bois, later teaching at McMaster University and serving as Director of the UBC Museum of Anthropology (1974–1997).
Michael M. Broido worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Cambridge from circa 1963 to 1969 and held a post at the University of Oxford.

Michael Meier-Brügger (born 1948) is a linguist who studied under Ernst Risch at the University of Zurich from circa 1967 to 1973. He held a post at the Free University of Berlin from circa 1996 to 2014.

Michael Oppitz (born 1942) works in Tibetology and other fields. He held positions at the Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin from circa 1987 to 1988 and served as Leiter at the University of Zurich from circa 1990 to 2008.
Michael P. Berman works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Attested in 2012, he served as a professor at Brock University and as managing editor of the Canadian Journal of Buddhist Studies.

Michael Pakenham Edgeworth (1812–1881) was an Indologist. He was educated at Charterhouse School and the University of Edinburgh (~1827–1829), and served in the Indian Civil Service from 1831 to 1859.

Michael Puett (born 1964) is a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1986–1994) studying under Marshall Sahlins and Anthony C. Yu, and has held professorships at Harvard University.

Michael Pye (born 1939) specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Cambridge under Maurice Wiles and earned a Ph.D. at Leeds, holding posts at Leeds, Marburg, Lancaster, and Otani University.

Michael Radich works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed a PhD at Harvard (~2001–2007) and studied at Kyoto University. His appointments include Victoria University of Wellington (2005–2017) and Professor of Buddhist Studies at Heidelberg University (2018).

Michael S. Drummond specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Bristol, where he earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies, and pursued doctoral studies at Utrecht University (attested 2006).

Michael Schmidt worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held appointments at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (1979, 1992, attested 2008), the Katalogisierung der orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland (1992), and the University of Göttingen (attested 1995).

Michael Schonken is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned an M.S. at California State University, Fullerton, taught at Beijing Royal School and Nord Anglia School Beijing, and became a Ph.D. student at Tsinghua University in 2024.

Michael Sheehy is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Steven D. Goodman at CIIS and Khenpo Kunga Sherab Salje Rinpoche. He held posts at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center and the University of Virginia.

Michael Silverstein (1945–2020) was a linguist. He studied at Stuyvesant High School (~1958–1961) and Harvard University (~1961–1971), and held a post at the University of Chicago from circa 1971 to 2020.

Michael Stanley-Baker works in Sinology and religious studies. He studied under Stephen R. Bokenkamp at Indiana University Bloomington, and has held posts at the Max Planck Institute, University of Leipzig, University of Pittsburgh, and Nanyang Technological University.
Michael Torsten Much (born 1953) is a scholar in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied as a fellow at the University of Hamburg and studied under Ernst Steinkellner.

Michael Viggo Fausbøll (1821–1908) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Hammerich, Johannsen, and Westergaard, later serving there as assistant librarian (1861) and professor (1878–1902).
